overview: Pannonhalma illuminates the role of Benedictine institutions in medieval Hungary through religious practice, buildings and long-lived community organization.

items.text: Pannonhalma was founded in 996 and participated in the spread of Christianity in Central Europe.
The monastery's community followed the Rule of St Benedict; monastic continuity is distinct from the kingdom's changing political arrangements.
Work on the present church began in 1224, incorporating remains of earlier structures.
The Late Gothic cloister dates to 1486. Later Baroque buildings and the nineteenth-century library belong to different chapters.

sources.title: UNESCO: Millenary Benedictine Abbey of Pannonhalma
